text:
Anya: FYI — observed a host-prefetch storm on node-7 after the v3 model rollout. PCIe queue saturates and tail stalls spike (~50ms). looks like aggressive speculative prefetching + high tenant concurrency.
Diego: can you paste the trace? was it mostly embeddings or attention KV?
Anya: mostly KV pages from long-context chat tenants. attached snippet from node logs: `dma_inflight=128 pcie_util=92% prefetch_aborts=14`
Riley: rough reproduction: when concurrency > 100 and prefetch_ahead >= 6, we see exponential growth in DMA ops. prefetches that never get used amplify pressure.
Kai: two orthogonal levers: (1) admission control for prefetch (limit inflight DMA per-node / per-tenant), (2) smarter prefetch candidate selection (predictive reuse score). I'd like to prototype (1) ASAP.
Diego: agree. for admission, propose token-pool per-node with two dimensions: dma_tokens and bandwidth_budget. tokens consumed per-page = estimated_bytes / token_size. token refill depends on observed pcie_util and dma_latency.
Anya: we also need a fast-fail path for critical tenants. if premium and latency-sensitive, allow bypass tokens but with hard rate cap.
Riley: predictor idea: track short-window reuse histogram per-address-prefix (128B/4KB bucket). compute a reuse_prob; prefetch only if reuse_prob * benefit_score > cost_threshold. very cheap estimator.
Kai: combine both: predictor provides a candidate list ordered by expected_gain; admission grants up to N DMA ops by priority until node budget exhausted. if budget exhausted, fallback is on-request fetch (maybe recompute) or deferred prefetch.
Diego: question: how to account for prefetches that get superseded (i.e., page evicted before use)? need cancellation and reclamation.
Riley: cancellation is best-effort. add a prefetch-id; eviction path can issue cancel to DMA queue if not started. reclamation metric tracks bytes_canceled and bytes_wasted.
Anya: sample config (draft):
```
prefetch_admission:
  node_budget_bytes: 128MB
  per_tenant_share_percent: 20
  dma_max_inflight: 64
  bypass_tokens:
    premium: {rate: 12MB/s, burst: 48MB}
    standard: {rate: 3MB/s, burst: 12MB}
  predictor:
    window_sec: 30
    reuse_threshold: 0.15
    prefix_bucket: 4KB
  cancel_grace_ms: 8
  deferred_retry_ms: 200
```
Kai: metrics to validate: `prefetch_inflight`, `prefetch_hit_rate`, `pcie_util_pct`, `dma_queue_latency_ms`, `prefetch_canceled_bytes`, `tail_latency_p99_by_tenant`
Diego: safety: introduce soft-mode where admission only throttles new prefetches but doesn't cancel existing ones. hard-mode enables cancellation if pcie_util > 95%. feature-flag both.
Anya: ops-bot: can we canary this on two staging nodes?
ops-bot: deploy-plan: canary prefetch-admission on cluster stg-gpu-2 (nodes 7-8) at 22:00 UTC. auto-rollback if p99 tail > 2x baseline for 10m.
Riley: dev tasks: (1) implement node token-pool + per-tenant accounting in offload-controller, (2) cheap reuse estimator in residency-proxy, (3) cancellation hooks in DMA worker.
Kai: long-term: consider integrating PCIe telemetry into the scheduler (NUMA-aware placement + batching) so prefetchs are aware of host topology. also evaluate prefetch vs recompute cost model for different model layers.
Diego: risks: estimator cold-start causes under-prefetch (affecting latency) or over-prefetch (resource storms). mitigation: safe defaults and adaptive learning with decay.
Anya: plan: Riley to draft short RFC with alg, config, and metrics. land admission as feature-flagged toggle behind `prefetch_admission=v1` and run canary.
Riley: will draft. ping me for review.
Anya: thanks — we'll sync after canary results. :rocket:
